Visit note | 2025-01-18 10:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Hafsa Munshi, 58, female. The patient presents with complaints of feeling lightheaded and experiencing fatigue with minimal exertion. She works as a lawyer and notes that these symptoms started after a sleepless night travelling to Tongi. She has no prior history of heart disease and denies chest pain, shortness of breath, or leg swelling. On examination: pulse 129 bpm and irregular, BP 131/74 mmHg, weight 88 kg. Her chest is clear on auscultation. Assessment: Atrial fibrillation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to limit tea and coffee, avoid alcohol, and report any fainting at once. Follow-up in 2 weeks with an ECG and kidney function tests.

Visit note | 2025-01-18 10:30 AM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Rezaul Molla, 56, male. Visit note | 2025-01-18 10:30 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Nabila Begum, 69, female. Visit note | 2025-01-18 11:30 AM | Dr. Rokeya Khatun, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Tasnim Ahmed, 24, female. Visit note | 2025-01-18 11:30 AM | Dr. Mahbuba Rahman, Psychiatry | Patient: Marium Howlader, 26, female. The patient presents seeking help for sudden episodes of a racing heart accompanied by shortness of breath, despite having normal cardiological investigations. Visit note | 2025-01-18 12:00 PM | Dr. Nasrin Sultana, Gastroenterology | Patient: Rina Dey, 51, female. Visit note | 2025-01-21 02:00 PM | Dr. Jannatul Ferdous, Orthopedics | Patient: Masud Gazi, 58, male. The patient presented to the clinic with complaints of persistent right knee pain that becomes particularly troublesome when climbing or descending stairs, a creaking sensation within the joint during movement, and mild morning stiffness that lasts for just a few minutes after waking up. He works as a garment merchandiser, which involves a moderate amount of standing and walking, but he reports that his knee symptoms became significantly worse after a long sightseeing trip on foot in Kamrangirchar where he walked several kilometers over uneven surfaces. He has no other chronic medical comorbidities. He denies any history of acute trauma, sudden swelling, popping sounds, locking of the knee joint, or systemic symptoms like fever and chills. He also reports no pain or stiffness in other major joints such as his hips, ankles, or wrists. On physical examination, his BMI is 27.2, and other vital signs are recorded as BP 113/79 mmHg, pulse 72 bpm, weight 65 kg. Musculoskeletal evaluation of the right knee reveals mild joint line tenderness along the medial aspect, palpable crepitus with active flexion and extension, and a slightly reduced range of motion due to discomfort, though there is no active joint effusion, erythema, or local warmth. Sensation and distal pulses in both lower limbs are completely intact, and his gait is antalgic but stable. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient was thoroughly counseled on the progressive nature of joint wear and the importance of lifestyle modifications. He was strongly advised to perform thigh-strengthening exercises, specifically quadriceps sets, daily to stabilize the joint, lose weight to decrease load on the articular cartilage, and strictly avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor, which can exacerbate joint stress and accelerate degeneration. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.
